Out of scope — the feature does not exist in this repository. This repo is the standalone wizard ('Brand Builder', app/page.tsx); the only routes are app/page.tsx and the three app/api/auth/* handlers. There is no theme listing page, no themes API, and no delete handler on any branch (checked main, hardening, suite-css-theme, suite-css-theme-clean). The Account settings listing lives in the wider suite, which the scope rules exclude. Needs: the suite's listing component and its delete endpoint.

Out of scope to fix — the Edit flow and its API live in the suite. BUT the diagnostic the ticket asks for is confirmed here, and the shape mismatch it predicts is real: 'Save Theme' writes a single localStorage key 'savedTheme' holding a nested 38-key object (app/page.tsx:2715, and identically at :5601 and :5678), while the load path (hooks/useThemeState.ts:61-107) reads ~38 separate flat keys ('themeColors', 'themeStyles', 'h1Font', ...) and never reads 'savedTheme' at all. Nothing in the repo reads it — it is write-only. Key names also disagree (payload 'colors'/'styles' vs loader 'themeColors'/'themeStyles'), and the payload omits themeName, themeType and linkWeight — the first two being exactly what a listing row would display. So a theme saved by the current version cannot be read back by it. Not patched: the serialisation shape is the contract with the suite's load endpoint, which is out of scope and not visible from here, so which shape is canonical needs a decision.

Root cause differs from the ticket. The name input already refuses an empty value (components/common/ThemeContextPanel.tsx:26-30), so 'saved with no name' is not reachable that way — the silently untitled themes come from the default 'Untitled Theme' the wizard starts with. The guard therefore treats both an empty name and the untouched default as missing. Flagging: this means a user cannot deliberately name a theme 'Untitled Theme'.

Root cause: a unit mismatch, not a missing mapping. Step 2 stores button padding unitless ('10'); the Step 4 overrides store it with the unit ('10px'). The preview appended 'px' unconditionally, so an override rendered as '10pxpx' and the browser dropped the declaration — which is why size, weight and border radius worked (they are not re-suffixed) and padding did not. Added toCssPx, which accepts either form. Verified in the browser: setting all four edges to 40/41/42/43 now yields a computed padding of '40px 41px 42px 43px'.

Step 3 and Step 4 each carried their own list; Step 4 offered only 300-800 with different labels (Regular/Semibold/Extrabold). Both now render from lib/font-weights.ts, the single source of truth, and getWeightLabel derives from it too. NO DATA MIGRATION NEEDED: every value Step 4 used to offer (300-800) is present in the shared 100-900 list, so themes saved against the old list still resolve — only the labels shown changed. Note the labels follow the casing spelled out in the ticket ('Extra light', 'Semi bold', 'Extra bold'), which differs from Step 3's previous 'Extra Light'/'Semi Bold'/'Extra Bold'. Verified in the browser: both steps now list the same nine options.

The ticket's hypothesis was half right. The generator and the checker DID already share the contrast maths, but not the large-text configuration: the generator called checkAllContrasts without a TextEvaluationConfig, so it took the default buttonLargeText=true and required only 3:1 for AA, while the checker computed it from the real 15px/600 button and required 4.5:1. Combinations landing between the two were offered as passing and then failed. Both now call one evaluateStyleContrast, and isLargeTextForWCAG moved into lib/wcag.ts. Also removed the duplicate luminance/contrast implementation from lib/styles.ts, which was a second copy waiting to drift. Test added at lib/wcag.test.mts using QA's palette, runnable with `pnpm test` (Node's built-in runner plus type stripping, no new dependencies); it records that 244 combinations from that palette would have been misclassified by the old code.
